summary: All six infra-perf items are implemented and checked on Build/infra-perf. (1) perf-02: each quality tier now has a render height cap (QualityTier.RenderScaleFor: Medium 1600 px, Low 1280 px, High none, or 1920 on Android). In the player only, LiquidRenderer applies it to the active URP renderScale when the renderer is created, when the tier changes and when Screen.height changes, and logs '[PainterIO] render scale ...'. ActorFieldCamera now takes its pixels per unit from the rendered height, so the actor RT shrinks along with the composite. (2) robust-02/perf-03: a watchdog frame longer than max(0.1 s, 4 frame budgets) resets the window and is not counted. Only non-attract rounds in Playing are measured, and only a non-attract session re-arms the one step. (3) robust-07: _PIO_Time is now seconds since the current session started and wraps at 4096 s, through LiquidRenderer.ShaderTimeFor. Only the comment changed in LiquidCommon.hlsl. (4) perf-09: the Builder sets Android blitType Auto and optimizedFramePacing on (ProjectSettings: androidBlitType 2, androidUseSwappy 1). (5) robust-09: PlayerSettings.runInBackground is off. Minimized in the menu, the release player now uses 2 ms of CPU per second, against 1315 on the Gate B build. (6) perf-01: verify.ps1 has an opt-in step 'perfslope', registered but not in the default run. It measures per-pixel shader cost per biome with the release probe (Medium tier, uncapped, 1080x1200 vs 540x600, best of 2 interleaved rounds). It PASSes or FAILs on fire/liquid > 1.6 or electric/liquid > 1.4. Runs from different agents are serialized by a lock. Each run waits for a quiet machine (no other PainterIO.exe and no Unity editor holding .unity.lock) and is retried if it shared the machine, within a 30 min budget. HOW TO RUN IT (the measurement tool for the fire, electric and liquid packages): pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/verify.ps1 -Steps perfslope -ProbeExe Build/<package>/PainterIO.exe -Agent <package> [-PerfRuns 3]. It prints one PASS/FAIL line with the three slopes in ms per Mpix and the two ratios. The per-run table is in Logs/<package>_perfslope.log, readable while it runs, and the player logs are in Logs/<package>_perfslope_<biome>_<WxH>_r<n>.log. It takes the perfslope lock, never the Unity lock. A run lasts about 12 minutes on a quiet machine; on a busy one, waiting and retries stop after 30 minutes and the remaining runs go at once, flagged. The slopes only mean something when no Unity editor and no other player is running. Baseline on the Gate B build (Build/Windows), measured while other agents were building: best-of-2 slopes liquid 2.58, fire 5.44, electric 3.33 ms per Mpix, so fire/liquid 2.11 (FAIL, as expected) and electric/liquid 1.29. Resumed run on Build/infra-perf (a 16:32 snapshot of the shared tree, quiet runs kept by the retries): PASS, liquid 2.00, fire 2.75, electric 1.60 ms per Mpix, fire/liquid 1.38, electric/liquid 0.80, hash unchanged. Probe hash 246577239DE179C4 is unchanged in every run. EditMode (from the run before the interruption; not rerun on resume because no infra-perf file changed since): 491 passing, the only failure is another package's mid-edit em dash check (biome-fire). PlayMode: 8/8. verify setup, probe, probe-fire, probe-electric and android: all PASS.

contract_issues: 12.4: tiers carry a render height cap: Medium 1600 px, Low 1280 px, High none (1920 on Android as 11.1). In the player (never in the editor) LiquidRenderer sets the active URP asset's renderScale = cap / Screen.height when the screen is taller than the cap, else 1, at creation, on a tier change and when Screen.height changes, and logs '[PainterIO] render scale <s> (tier <t>, height <h>)'. GameDirector's 11.1 Android 1920 cap stays and gives the same value on High (it is now redundant).

12.2 item 2 / 19 (actor field): RT size = view size x ppu x tier scale, where ppu now comes from the rendered height (main camera pixelHeight x URP renderScale clamped to 0.1-1), with the RtQuantum (32 px) rounding.

12.4: frames longer than max(0.1 s, 4 frame budgets) reset the watchdog window and are not counted; only real rounds (not the attract) in the Playing state are measured; only a non-attract session start re-arms the at-most-one step. The rest of 12.4 is unchanged (5 s warm-up, 3 s window, 0.83 x target, never when the target is <= 30).

Shader globals (LiquidCommon.hlsl, B1 table): _PIO_Time.x = unscaled seconds since the current session started (reset on every GameDirector.SessionStarted: round start, REJOUER, menu return, attract restart), wrapping at 4096 s; it was app time wrapped at 1024 s.

17: PlayerSettings.runInBackground = false (PlayerProbe, DevShot and RenderLab set Application.runInBackground = true at runtime); Android PlayerSettings.Android.blitType = Auto and optimizedFramePacing = true (ProjectSettings androidBlitType 2, androidUseSwappy 1).

18.4: verify.ps1 gains the opt-in step perfslope (registered, never in the default order): release probe -quality medium -fps 1000 -mute windowed at 1080x1200 and 540x600 per biome, -PerfRuns interleaved rounds, slope = (best avgMs big - best avgMs small) / 0.972 ms per Mpix, FAIL when fire/liquid > 1.6 or electric/liquid > 1.4, a run fails, the tier is not Medium or the probe hashes differ; serialized across agents by Logs/perfslope.lock; waits for no other PainterIO.exe and no .unity.lock before each run and retries a shared run (240 s quiet wait per run, 2 retries, 30 min budget).

items.evidence: QualityTier.RenderScaleFor/RenderHeightCap, LiquidRenderer.ApplyRenderScale (#if !UNITY_EDITOR; called at Build, in OnTierChanged and from LateUpdate when Screen.height changes; logs once per change), ActorFieldCamera ppu from RenderedHeight(main.pixelHeight, URP renderScale clamped 0.1-1) with QuantizeSide kept. WaveC_RenderScaleFor_Table PASS: (2400, Medium, android) 0.6667, (2400, Low) 0.5333, (2400, High, android) 0.8, (1920, Medium) 0.8333, (960, Medium, PC) 1, (1200, High, PC) 1, plus the edges. WaveC_ActorField_FollowsTheRenderedHeight PASS (1080x2400 Medium: RT height 1248 -> 832). Gate_ActorFieldSizeStaysPutDuringTheChaseZoom PASS. Release check: -screen-height 1600 is clamped to 1200 by this 1920x1200 monitor (docs/waveC/infra-perf/renderscale_low_720x1600: 'render scale 1.000 (tier Low, height 1200)'). So the window of a -quality low probe run was resized to a 720x1600 client with MoveWindow (docs/waveC/infra-perf/tools/tallwindow.ps1). The player logged '[PainterIO] render scale 0.800 (tier Low, height 1600)', the actor field became 224x480, and the probe PASSed with hash 246577239DE179C4. Screenshots docs/waveC/infra-perf/renderscale_low_1600/cut.png and results.png: the composite is smooth after the bilinear upscale and the HUD and results text stay native and crisp. Not yet checked on a real Android device.

QualityTier.TickWatchdog: outlier frames (IsOutlierFrame, > max(0.1 s, 4/target)) call ResetWindow and are not counted. LiquidRenderer.LateUpdate: running also requires !s.IsAttract and director.State == Playing. OnSessionStarted calls BeginSession only for non-attract sessions. Tests PASS: WaveC_Watchdog_OneHitchDoesNotStep (60 fps with a 1.5 s frame at t = 12 s: no step), WaveC_Watchdog_SteadyLowRateStepsOnce (40 fps for 9 s: exactly one step High -> Medium, still one after 9 s more), WaveC_Watchdog_NotRunningNeverSteps, WaveC_Watchdog_OutlierThreshold, WaveC_Watchdog_SlowFramesAroundAHitchStillStep. Release checks on Build/infra-perf: the critic's menu hitch run (process suspended 1.5 s at t = 12 s, focused window) gives no watchdog line (docs/waveC/infra-perf/hitch_menu/result.txt). The idle-menu-then-minimized run gives no watchdog line (docs/waveC/infra-perf/minimize). A 1.5 s suspension 8 s into the probe's real bot round (Auto tier, -fps 60) gives no watchdog line and the probe PASSes (docs/waveC/infra-perf/hitch_round). The same hitch on the Gate B build logs 'quality watchdog: 29,9 fps < 49,8, tier High -> Medium' (docs/waveC/infra-perf/hitch_round_gateB_control), so the check tells the two builds apart.

LiquidRenderer.PublishFrameGlobals sends ShaderTimeFor(Time.unscaledTimeAsDouble, timeEpoch), (now - epoch) % 4096, never negative. timeEpoch is set in Build and reset in OnSessionStarted. Only the _PIO_Time comment changed in LiquidCommon.hlsl. WaveC_ShaderTime_CountsFromTheSessionAndWraps PASS: ShaderTimeFor(e, e) = 0, ShaderTimeFor(e + 5000, e) = 904 < 4096. ShaderCheck PASS on 12 shaders, the Android APK built and compiled the GLES3/Vulkan variants, and verify probe/probe-fire/probe-electric PASS on Build/infra-perf with hash 246577239DE179C4.

Minimized release player in the menu (method of docs/waveC/robust-refute/minimize, tools/hitch.ps1 -Mode minimize, window focused first): visible 542 ms/s, minimized 2 ms/s = 0.2 % of one core, below the 5 % target (docs/waveC/infra-perf/minimize/result.txt). Gate B control: visible 1215 ms/s, minimized 1315 ms/s, and the watchdog even stepped in the menu (docs/waveC/infra-perf/minimize_gateB_control/result.txt).

tools/verify.ps1 has the step 'perfslope' in $StepTable but not in $DefaultSteps. '-List' still shows the same default order. It writes one PASS/FAIL line and logs under Logs/<agent>_perfslope*.log. 'pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/verify.ps1 -Steps perfslope -Agent infra-perf-baseline' on the current Build/Windows (Logs/infra-perf-baseline_perfslope.log, all 12 probe runs PASS, hash 246577239DE179C4) printed 'FAIL perfslope: slopes liquid=3.69 fire=9.49 electric=3.14; fire/liquid=2.57 (max 1.6)'. That run used the mean of the rounds and 11 of the 12 runs overlapped a Unity editor. The same table under the shipped best-of-rounds estimator gives liquid 2.58, fire 5.44, electric 3.33, so fire/liquid 2.11 (FAIL as expected) and electric/liquid 1.29, close to the plan's 2.06 / 1.38. A second run on Build/infra-perf while four other agents' players and Unity builds ran gave unusable numbers (liquid slope -1.01). The step refused it ('liquid slope is not positive') and flagged the noisy sizes. That run led to the quiet-machine wait, the retries and the 30 min budget. The biome-fire package's run (Logs/biome-fire_perfslope.log) exercises them, including the takeover of a stale perfslope lock. An offline self-test that loads the step from the verify.ps1 AST with a fake player (scratchpad, not shipped) checks the aggregation. Fed docs/waveC/perf/probe_matrix.txt, it gives liquid 2.26, fire 4.38, electric 3.01, so fire/liquid 1.94 (FAIL) and electric/liquid 1.33 (PASS); the plan's 2.06 / 1.38 came from means. A contended run is retried and only the quiet value counts. Resumed run (18:51-19:15, after the workflow was interrupted): 'pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/verify.ps1 -Steps perfslope -ProbeExe Build/infra-perf/PainterIO.exe -Agent infra-perf' took over the stale perfslope lock left by biome-fire's interrupted run (dead PID 30880) and printed 'PASS perfslope: slopes ms/Mpix (medium, uncapped) liquid=2.00 fire=2.75 electric=1.60; fire/liquid=1.38 (max 1.6); electric/liquid=0.80 (max 1.4); hash 246577239DE179C4; 22 runs (13 shared the machine with another player or a Unity editor, 7 of them with a Unity editor)' in 1435 s, OVERALL PASS, exit 0 (Logs/infra-perf_perfslope.log). The machine was quiet for the first 5 minutes; then the other resumed agents started Unity, and the retries kept a quiet run for every size (best quiet avgMs: liquid 3.28 / 1.34, fire 4.44 / 1.77, electric 3.45 / 1.89 ms at 1080x1200 / 540x600). Caveat: Build/infra-perf was compiled at 16:32 from the shared source tree, so it already contains the biome packages' edits of that moment (ElectricBead.hlsl and ElectricOverlay.hlsl at 16:21-16:22, FireFx.cs at 16:32). These slopes are neither the Gate B baseline nor the final biome numbers. 'verify -List' still shows the unchanged default order.

open_issues: Perf numbers on this shared laptop are only meaningful when no Unity editor and no other player run (on the integrated Iris Xe, CPU load from a build alone slowed the probe frames 2 to 4 times). perfslope now waits for that and flags what it could not get, but the gate should take the reference slopes when the wave's agents are done.

While stopping my own perfslope run at 17:15 I also killed the biome-fire agent's verify process, which was waiting on the perfslope lock (my process filter matched 'perfslope'). Their agent restarted it at 17:16 and its run took over the stale lock correctly. Any biome-fire perf result started before 17:16 is void.

With runInBackground off, a release player started without focus (for example by a script, with no -probe or -devshot) stays paused until it is focused. That is expected, but hand-run 'plain player' checks by other packages must focus the window first (tools/hitch.ps1 shows the Alt + SetForegroundWindow way).

GameDirector's Android 1920 px cap (game-flow file) is now redundant with LiquidRenderer.ApplyRenderScale. It is harmless and gives the same value; it can be removed together with a contract 11.1 update in a later wave.

Reference slopes on a quiet machine are still pending for the gate. The resumed run measured Build/infra-perf (liquid 2.00, fire 2.75, electric 1.60 ms per Mpix; fire/liquid 1.38, electric/liquid 0.80, PASS). That build is a 16:32 snapshot of the shared tree that already contains some biome shader edits, and 13 of its 22 runs shared the machine (the retries kept a quiet run for every size). The Gate B build (Build/Windows) was not measured again on a quiet machine, so the plan's probe_matrix baselines remain the reference.
